outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms are expected on Wednesday from the Mid Missouri Valley into Wisconsin. A few tornadoes, hail, and wind are expected. Isolated hail cannot be ruled out extending south across Missouri and into Arkansas.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: A compact but intense shortwave trough will move from Kansas at 12Z Wednesday into Iowa by 00Z with 100 kt midlevel speed max spreading across Missouri, Iowa, and into Wisconsin. Similarly, a surface low will develop from Kansas into Iowa during the day, with quasi-stationary front from northern Wisconsin into southern Minnesota north of the low. Backing and strengthening southerly 850 mb flow will enhance low-level shear profiles ahead of the low, with sufficient destabilization expected across the region to support scattered severe storms including the threat for several tornadoes. Aforementioned wave will move into the Upper Great Lakes overnight, with surface low gradually filling across Wisconsin and Michigan. ...Mid Missouri Valley northeastward into southern Minnesota and Wisconsin... As of this writing, an extensive area of rain and thunderstorms stretches from Nebraska across Iowa. With time, this should all lift northward, setting the stage for destabilization via heating during the day on Wednesday. sections.title: Missouri into Arkansas
sections.text: A few thunderstorms are expected early Wednesday along a cold front, from eastern Oklahoma southward into Texas. This activity is not expected to be severe, and should experience a weakening trend by late morning. To the east, a marginally unstable air mass will remain, but the shortwave trough will be lifting well to the north. Overall, forcing for ascent across southern Missouri and Arkansas will be weak, but isolated thunderstorms cannot be ruled out. As such, will maintain a low-end severe risk for mainly hail. ..Jewell/Cook.. 05/17/2017

outlooks.summary: Severe storms are expected to develop this afternoon from the Mid Missouri Valley into Wisconsin. A few tornadoes, large hail, and strong wind gusts are possible. Farther south, at least a marginal severe risk will extend south across southern Missouri and into Arkansas.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: Within the broader synoptic trough, a compact shortwave trough over western KS will eject northeast into the middle to upper MS Valley region, while an upstream upper low settles southward into the great basin. Surface low associated with the leading shortwave trough is now located over western KS. This feature will develop northeast along a southwest-northeast oriented stationary front through eastern NE and IA today while trailing Pacific front continues into the mid MS Valley and southern Plains where it will likely stall.

sections.title: Upper Mississippi Valley and Great Lakes region
sections.text: Cluster of elevated storms over north-central KS has developed along and north of the stationary front, within zone of forced ascent/DPVA accompanying the compact shortwave trough. These storms will pose a marginal hail threat. Otherwise widespread multi-layer clouds and areas of showers/thunderstorms are evident this morning within belt of ascent along warm conveyor from eastern KS, through MO, the upper MS Valley and Great Lakes. However, WV imagery indicates a dry slot from OK into central KS wrapping around the southern and eastern periphery of the shortwave trough. The dry slot will shift northeast and contribute to potential for partial clearing and diabatic warming in a portion of warm sector with 1000-1500 J/kg MLCAPE likely. As the atmosphere destabilizes, strong DPVA accompanying the negative-tilt, ejecting shortwave trough will support additional thunderstorm development along arcing convergence bands. Both discrete modes and bowing segments are likely. Storms will be embedded within strong 45+ kt surface-6 km shear supportive of supercells and bowing segments. Additionally, 0-1 km hodograph size will increase as the low-level jet strengthens in this region, supporting p

sections.title: Middle to lower Mississippi Valley region
sections.text: With stronger forcing for ascent associated with the ejecting shortwave trough likely to remain north of this region, storm coverage will probably be limited. Nevertheless, strong deep-layer shear will reside in warm sector where the atmosphere should become moderately unstable as the boundary layer warms. Any storms developing in this environment may organize and pose a severe threat. ..Dial/Edwards.. 05/17/2017

outlooks.summary: Severe storms are expected to develop this afternoon from the Mid Missouri Valley into Wisconsin. A few tornadoes, large hail, and strong wind gusts are possible. Farther south, at least a marginal severe risk will extend south across southern Missouri and possibly into Arkansas.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: While ridging aloft persists across the eastern U.S. through the period, a large/long-wave trough will reside over the western and central portions of the country. This trough will remain comprised of two main pieces -- a closed low digging southeast across the Intermountain west, and second/weaker lead low and associated negatively tilted short-wave trough, moving quickly northeastward out of the central Plains toward the upper Mississippi Valley area. At the surface, a low -- nearly co-located with the center of upper circulation currently crossing central Kansas per WV loop -- is expected to move northeast across the mid-Missouri Valley into IA this afternoon, and then into the upper Great Lakes region overnight. Trailing south from the low, a weakening baroclinic zone will shift across Kansas into Iowa/Missouri through the afternoon, with bands of strong/severe thunderstorms developing starting early this afternoon in advance of this system. ...Mid-Missouri Valley into the Upper Great Lakes, and southward across the Ozarks... outlooks.summary: Severe storms are expected to impact portions of the mid Missouri Valley into the Upper Midwest late this afternoon into evening. Some of this activity may become capable of producing very large hail and tornadoes, a couple of which could be strong, particularly across parts of northern and eastern Iowa.

sections.title: 20Z Outlook Update
sections.text: Categorical and probabilistic lines have been adjusted some, particularly across parts of the mid Missouri Valley into the Upper Midwest, to account for the latest trends in model output and observational data. Higher severe hail and tornado probabilities have been extended westward into northwestern Iowa, in closer proximity to the surface low center. These same probabilities have been lowered across parts of northeastern Kansas and northwestern Missouri, where near surface flow has veered to a more southwesterly component to the south of the low, and mixing has lowered surface dew points. An increase in storm development does now appear underway across Iowa, as the mid-level cold core begins pivoting across the region, before becoming increasingly deformed and weakening in an increasingly confluent regime across the Upper Midwest later this evening. With southerly 850 mb winds in the process of increasing to 40-50 kt within the warm sector across eastern Iowa, in the presence of increasing boundary layer instability (CAPE to 1500+ J/kg), the environment may become favorable for a couple of supercells capable of producing very large hail and tornadoes, one or two of which could be

outlooks.summary: Severe storms will continue to impact parts of the mid to upper Mississippi Valley this evening into tonight. The threat for damaging wind gusts will be greatest across eastern Iowa, northwest Illinois and southwest Wisconsin. Large hail and a couple brief tornadoes will also be possible across the mid to upper Mississippi this evening.

sections.title: Mid to Upper Mississippi Valley
sections.text: Water vapor imagery shows a negatively tilted upper-level trough over the mid Missouri Valley with a band of large-scale ascent moving northeastward across the upper Mississippi Valley. At the surface, a 993 mb low is moving northeastward across northwest Iowa with a corridor of low-level moisture ahead of the low extending northward from Illinois into Wisconsin and southeastern Minnesota. Several line segments are ongoing along this corridor with one line in north-central Wisconsin and another near the Mississippi River in far eastern Iowa. The latest RAP shows moderate instability ahead of this activity with MLCAPE values across much of Iowa and northern Illinois estimated in the 1200 to 1800 J/kg range. In addition, the RAP shows a 65 to 80 kt mid-level jet over the mid Mississippi Valley with the left exit region of this feature located across eastern parts of the upper Mississippi Valley. The exit region of the jet is enhancing lift and deep-layer shear across the Upper Mississippi Valley where 0-6 km shear values are estimated in the 45 to 55 kt range. This will be enough to maintain a wind damage threat with line segments that can persist this evening and into the early over

sections.title: Arkansas/Missouri and central Illinois
sections.text: Southwest flow will remain in place across the Ozarks and mid Mississippi Valley this evening into tonight. An axis of moderate instability is currently analyzed by the RAP from the Arklatex northeastward into eastern Missouri where MLCAPE values are estimated in the 1500 to 2000 J/kg range. Moderate instability should remain in place across the region as warm advection is maintained due to veering winds in the low-levels. This may allow for isolated convective initiation along the instability axis during the late evening or in the early overnight period. NAM forecast soundings in the Ozarks around midnight show 0-6 km shear in the 50 to 60 kt range and show potential for surface-based convection. This could be enough for a marginal wind damage or hail threat. ..Broyles.. 05/18/2017

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe thunderstorms are expected to develop ahead of a migratory low in northeast KS, then spread into IA. Isolated tornadoes are expected along with large hail and damaging winds.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Exit region of strong mid-level jet is rapidly spreading across northeast KS late this morning. As 90kt+ 500mb speed max translates into northwest MO by 18z large-scale forcing for ascent will shift into IA. Mid-high level cloudiness has cleared nicely ahead of this feature and strong boundary-layer heating is observed ahead of the surface low. Diagnostic data suggests surface-3km lapse rates are now in excess of 8 C/km across northeast KS and further steepening is expected along a corridor extending into IA as high clouds clear. Latest visible satellite imagery suggests boundary-layer cu field is thickening immediately ahead of surface drying from eastern KS, arcing toward southeast NE. While deep convection is evolving along the trailing cold front, latest thinking is discrete supercells will evolve ahead of the front then track northeast into an increasingly buoyant air mass. Isolated tornadoes are expected, along with hail and wind.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorms will move into the area in the next hour. The main threat is marginally severe hail, but severe wind gusts are possible as a line segment continues to organize. Conditions will be monitored for a weather watch in the next few hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A small band of storms with the potential for marginally severe hail will be moving into the region in the next hour. Although the main warm front is north of the area, the storms are likely elevated given the substantial MLCIN and little MLCAPE in northeast IA at the moment. However, with the ongoing heating, the storms will likely became more surface-based with time as suggested by RAP forecast soundings. A narrow plume of somewhat steep lapse rates currently extending southward from the ongoing storms is expected to advect quickly into Wisconsin given the persistence of strong southerly flow in the 850-500 mb layer. Given the above factors, along with substantial boundary layer moisture (dewpoints in the mid 60s), the ongoing storms are expected to continue their intensity as they move northeast in the next few hours. Given bulk deep-layer shear of 40-55 kt, and the similar orientation of the mean winds and the deep-layer wind shear vector, an organized small convective system may continue to organize and strengthen. Initially, severe hail is the main threat, but as the boundary layer warms and the convection organizes, severe wind gusts will be possible. Additional initiation of storms is expected to occur to the south of the ongoing storms, but will likely hold off until after 1830 UTC, and therefore a watch is not expected to be issued until after then.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Greatest tornado threat appears to be shifting to the northern half of WW231.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Surface low has moved quickly into east-central NE, just northwest of OMA. Substantial boundary-layer drying has advected northeast across KS into western MO where surface dew points have lowered into the low-mid 50s. This drying should continue as south-southwesterly winds are gusting well in excess of 40kt across southeast KS/southwest MO. In response to large-scale forcing shifting into the mid MS Valley, boundary-layer moisture will likely hold across the northern half of IA into southern WI. It appears the most robust convection will focus along a corridor from southeast NE...northeast toward southwest WI. Numerous showers/thunderstorms are evolving within this zone and discrete supercells should mature over the next few hours. Tornado threat should increase across this region, along and south of synoptic front draped from northwest IA into southeast MN. ..Darrow.. 05/17/2017 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A band of thunderstorms are increasing in intensity across northeast IA and will pose the threat for severe wind/hail, along with the potential for a few tornadoes. A tornado watch is likely to be issued in the next 60-90 minutes.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Although the area has been under a thin cirrus shield the last few hours, heating into the upper 70s to low 80s, along with dewpoints holding generally in the mid 60s, has destabilized the area substantially over the last few hours. Strong forcing and cold mid-level temperatures aloft from the approaching upper low is now impacting the western portion of the area as seen by the band of thunderstorms arcing from FXV to FFL. Deep-layer shear is more than sufficient for organized storms. Deep, moist profiles in the lower troposphere, as identified in the 18z OAX and DVN soundings, should prevent larger-scale cold pools from developing the next few hours, and therefore discrete convective modes and/or small bowing line segments are expected to continue. Although the deep-layer shear is mostly unidirectional out of the south, subtle backing of low-level winds seen over much of the area which will contribute to some potential for low-level rotation and a few tornadoes in the stronger updrafts. Given the above factors a tornado watch will likely be needed in the next 60-90 minutes.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Tornado watch will likely be issued by 21z for portions of eastern IA and northwest IL.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Buoyancy has gradually increased across eastern IA and northwest IL this afternoon where MLCAPE values are now on the order of 1000 J/kg. CINH has decreased and thunderstorms are gradually maturing well ahead of strong negative-tilt short-wave trough. While substantial low-level drying has surged across MO it appears near-60F surface dew points should hold across this region. Severe threat is increasing across this region and a new tornado watch is warranted to account for expected supercell development.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Scattered to widespread severe gusts are forecast with a bowing thunderstorm band over eastern portions of IA and this feature will move into southeastern MN and southwest WI this evening.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A mature and well-developed QLCS arcs from north-central IA into east-central and southeastern IA and it is moving north-northeast at 50-55 kt. The convective band is on the leading edge of a mid-level dryslot punching northeastward into the middle-upper MS Valley in the base of a migratory shortwave trough. Surface temperatures ahead of the squall line have warmed into the upper 70s to around 80 degrees F over much of the discussion area. Marshalltown IA (KMIW) recorded a measured gust of 60-kt at 2212Z and Waterloo, IA (KALO) more recently observed a 61-kt gust at 2253Z. Expecting the QLCS to continue to result in scattered to widespread severe gusts (60-75 kt). Single site radar imagery has also indicated the development of a couple of substantial mesovortices in the squall line. A couple of short-track weak tornadoes are possible with any sustained/stronger mesovortex which appear to be most likely over northeast IA into adjacent portions of MN/WI over the next 1-2 hours. ..Smith.. 05/17/2017 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe threat is expected to continue across central and east-central WI for the next few hours. All severe hazards, including tornadoes, are possible.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Current (2315Z) radar imagery shows several supercells embedded in the southern portion of the convective line moving northeastward across central WI. Recent surface analysis places the warm front near RGK east-northeastward to north of MNM. Thermodynamic environment along and north of this front is only weakly unstable with convective inhibition building over the past hour. However, the thermodynamic environment south of the front, which includes much of central and east-central WI, is characterized by temperatures in the mid to upper 70s, dewpoints in the low to mid 60s, and MLCAPE over 1000 J/kg (per the latest mesoanalysis). The immediate downstream kinematic environment is characterized by a veering wind profile composed of relatively weak southeasterly surface winds increasing to over 40 kt from the south-southwest at 850 mb and over 60 kt from the southwest at 500mb. Overall, the downstream environment across central and east-central WI is supportive of a continued severe threat for at least the next few hours. All severe hazards, including tornadoes, are possible across the remainder of Tornado Watch 223. ..Mosier.. 05/17/2017 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The squall line over northwest IL will move into northeast IL later this evening. Isolated severe gusts are possible.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Radar mosaic shows a broken line of cells to the east of the Quad Cities with a continuous squall line over parts of northern IL into south-central WI. The boundary layer has been slow to cool this evening in part to considerable mixing with temperatures slowly falling from the upper 70s into the middle 70s degrees F and dewpoints are around 60 F. The KLOT VAD has shown an increase in 0.5-2.0 km flow and hodographs have become quite large. Although the tornado risk is thought to be low, a nonzero risk for a brief/weak tornado may accompany any updraft with persistent rotation. Isolated gusts 50-65 mph are possible with the stronger downdrafts which would result in wind damage.
